deliverable: Persistent g += P schedule verified end to end on Ascend950PR, with V buffer lifetime, D-tail, CN-tail/all-invalid row and prefetch safety each checked by positive AND negative tests.

root_cause.cause: A shared (UB) buffer filled BEFORE a persistent T.Pipelined loop does not hold its contents in later iterations. The resident gamma/w staging established outside the loop is stale from iteration 1 onward. Re-establishing residency INSIDE the iteration is correct.
root_cause.why_it_masqueraded_as_state_carry: the running m/l/acc state in st[] was never the problem, and the G52 bisection that narrowed the symptom to 'a second reducer in one VF region' was narrowing a SYMPTOM: two reducers over the same quantity pass.

discriminating_experiments.finding: two reducers over the SAME quantity (vf*vf) in one region PASS
discriminating_experiments.implication: the second reducer itself is not the cause

discriminating_experiments.finding: second reducer reading shared g_ub FAILS
second reducer reading shared w_ub PASSES
discriminating_experiments.implication: not any shared read; g_ub is the FIRST buffer written before the loop, so the LEADING residency region is what goes stale

discriminating_experiments.finding: g_ub staged into a fragment before reducing STILL FAILS
discriminating_experiments.implication: it is g_ub's VALUE that is wrong, not how it is read

discriminating_experiments.finding: residency kept with buffer versions pinned to 1 FAILS

also_rejected: loop-invariant code motion hoisting the state init (an iteration-dependent init, and one built from a per-iteration MEMORY value, both failed identically)
a missing cross-iteration sync (an explicit PIPE_ALL barrier changed nothing)
shared-buffer reuse across iterations (allocating inside the loop changed nothing; alloc_shared hoists to function scope regardless)
nested Pipelined constructs (fully unrolling the inner loop changed nothing)
a simple index fault (the wrong values match no other token's expected output)
root_cause.my_own_test_bug_worth_recording: the first persistent run reported all rows bad; the cause was MY test reference including the alpha blend while the kernel finalize did not. The kernel was fine. Recorded because the mirror-image mistake -- trusting a passing comparison that was never checked -- is how a wrong kernel gets committed.

persistent_schedule.form: grid = P programs; group g = pid + it*P over ceil(M/P) iterations; residency re-established inside each iteration

synthetic_verification.note: odd grid and a D tail

d_tail.measured_behaviour: the device kernel stages exactly D elements per copy and masks every VF loop with i < D, so a D tail (2047, 1000, 257, 100) is correct at the real D

invalid_rows.hazard: Two DIFFERENT 'all-invalid row' cases exist and conflating them was a real error in this module's first version. (a) masked_zero: every D lane masked to 0, so v=0, rms=sqrt(eps), key=0 and the SCORE IS 0 -- finite; the depth softmax is uniform and agg=0, so the output is the residual branch (1-alpha)*x. This is the case a device actually meets and it is SAFE. (b) neg_inf: the score is FORCED to -inf for every block, and then m - score = -inf - -inf = NaN is a real hazard.
invalid_rows.guard: a FINITE floor (the measured kernel uses -1e30) applied before the subtraction, so the neg_inf hazard is arithmetic rather than a special case

rules_and_their_negative_tests.prevents: the neg_inf policy not being applied to every block (and must NOT fire for masked_zero, where a finite score is correct)
a NaN reaching l and the output
the 0/0 division a fully -inf row leaves behind even with a finite floor

two_findings_from_this_modules_own_tests.why_it_matters: a guard SHOULD yield bet = 0 for a fully-invalid block; treating exp(-inf) as a failure would reject a correct guard, while treating a NaN difference as 0 would accept a broken one. The two are now distinguished by an explicit _safe_exp.
two_findings_from_this_modules_own_tests.how_found: a negative test asserted safety for an all-invalid row and the module reported a violation

two_findings_from_this_modules_own_tests.finding: a finite floor is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT
two_findings_from_this_modules_own_tests.why_it_matters: if every block scores -inf then bet = 0 at every step, l stays exactly 0, and the final acc/l is 0/0. The denominator needs its own guard; rule invalid_row_zero_denominator records it.
two_findings_from_this_modules_own_tests.how_found: the helper function returned bet = 0 and the divergence of l to 0 became visible only after exp(-inf) was handled correctly

slots that can never hold distinct blocks

two in-flight loads sharing one buffer

prefetch.outer_prefetch: group_prefetch_target(g, P) = g + P, stated as a function because that sum is the entire requirement and an off-by-one would prefetch the group being computed
prefetch.depth_measured: single-slot is the only depth with device evidence; multi-slot is checked structurally and pruned on UB, NOT measured

tests.coverage: every rule has a positive and a deliberately-broken negative case

not_claimed: Multi-slot V prefetch depth 2/3 on device: checked structurally and pruned against UB, but NOT executed.
Any performance claim: no cycle timings, no bandwidth figure, no prefetch-depth speedup. G51 is a safety and correctness gate here.
A fully-invalid token row on device: the NaN guard is demonstrated arithmetically and checked by rule, not executed as a device case.
Physical synchronisation equivalence: the lifetime rules are dataflow predicates, not a proof about hardware event ordering.
